title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
content: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

title: Governing African Economies as They Are
content: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

title: Making Earth Cool Again
content: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
content: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

title: China Ratchets Up Its Weaponization of Trade
content: Just as the US has been leveraging its large market and technological leadership for geopolitical ends, China is now using its dominance in critical minerals, industrial inputs, and specialized manufacturing machinery to coerce and punish other countries. The consequences, both economic and geopolitical, are far-reaching.

title: There Is Only One Thing to Talk About With Russia
content: The European security order’s foundational principle is never to tolerate aggression. There is no need to revise that order, as the Kremlin has proposed, only to wait for a Russian regime that is willing to respect other countries’ territorial integrity and uphold its own previous commitments.

title: The Truth About Global AI Governance
content: Because the current approach to global AI governance presumes that developing countries are full of eager adopters of AI who need to be cautioned about the technology's risks, it overlooks what their information environments and media markets actually need. A survey of researchers who study 71 countries sets the record straight.

title: Demography is the Achilles’ Heel of Dictatorships
content: Governments that manipulate population figures often end up deceiving themselves as much as the public. When autocratic leaders mistake inflated numbers for real national strength, they make costly strategic mistakes and fail to address their countries’ demographic decline until it is too late.

title: The Silver Lining of a Data-Center Slowdown
content: With leading AI labs under intense competitive pressure to keep advancing the frontier of the technology's capabilities, resistance to the build-out of computing resources is not such a bad thing. The more time we can buy, the greater our chances of maximizing the potential benefits and mitigating the risks.

title: What Nvidia’s Crisis Reveals About the Chip War
content: Export restrictions, like those depriving China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, may buy time by curtailing a competitor's access to frontier capabilities made elsewhere. But in any technological conflict, policymakers must remember that slowing a rival is not the same as strengthening oneself.

title: When Export Restraints Are the Lesser Evil
content: Governments face pressure to protect domestic industries while preserving access to cheaper foreign goods. The recent EU-China car-export deal offers an uneasy compromise that protects European automakers while keeping Chinese cars available to consumers, making it preferable to prohibitive tariffs.

title: The Trade Losses That Nobody Counts
content: While much of the United Kingdom’s post-Brexit debate has focused on the monetary value of lost trade with the European Union, the composition of UK-EU trade flows warrants closer attention. A sharp decline in the variety of products shipped to Europe suggests that the economic costs have been greater than many realize.

title: Nigeria’s Big Bet on Health Care
content: Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and medical equipment leaves families exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations and hospitals at the mercy of global supply chains. Expanding domestic manufacturing is essential to reducing the cost of treatment and ensuring that more Nigerians can access quality care.

title: What Should the Nvidia Board Do?
content: The proper role of any corporate board is to strike a careful balance between stakeholders. In Nvidia's case, the board will have to consider not just the current trading price, but also how its decisions will affect the landscape in which it operates, its employees, and its license to trade.

title: The Roots of Macron’s Failure
content: Although French President Emmanuel Macron has certainly made mistakes, his troubled presidency is symptomatic of a deeper problem. In the end, he failed to build something truly enduring because he was seduced by the same monarchical impulse that is a recurring feature of French political culture.

title: The Perverse Effects of the AI Investment Boom
content: As big tech companies increasingly turn to debt markets to finance massive investments in AI data centers, they are competing for the same pools of capital as many governments. With interest rates already high and public demands for spending on the rise, the timing could hardly be worse for vulnerable economies.

title: What Adam Smith Missed
content: For all that he got right, the "founding father" of economics failed to see how technological innovations lead to market monopolization. If AI is left to the invisible hand, it will almost certainly increase economic and political inequality, causing even deeper social polarization and further undermining democracy.

title: Oceania’s Three Goals for COP31
content: To make COP31 the “Blue COP,” delegates must recommit to keeping the 1.5° Celsius warming goal alive, reform the climate-finance system, and address our dependence on the fossil fuels driving the ocean's warming and acidification. Pacific countries have long championed these causes, but now the rest of the world must join them.
